### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d6ec91d2f89e834fc5b82183a95cb3c5427a882`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d6ec91d2f89e834fc5b82183a95cb3c5427a882` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ac9fa98c9d9bba4bd4ce8bd0401235514670fdbb` — the merge of head `978ce6133f3eb9332b3aae99564553d99803540f` into base `7d6ec91d2f89e834fc5b82183a95cb3c5427a882`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ac9fa98c9d9bba4bd4ce8bd0401235514670fdbb && git checkout ac9fa98c9d9bba4bd4ce8bd0401235514670fdbb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7d6ec91d2f89e834fc5b82183a95cb3c5427a882 978ce6133f3eb9332b3aae99564553d99803540f && git checkout -B drift-repro 7d6ec91d2f89e834fc5b82183a95cb3c5427a882 && git merge --no-ff 978ce6133f3eb9332b3aae99564553d99803540f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d6ec91d2f89e834fc5b82183a95cb3c5427a882
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7d6ec91d2f89e834fc5b82183a95cb3c5427a882` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `marchtian` · `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH` · 2026-10-17T15:56Z · head `3e1faaeafe`. It lands through the merge queue once every check on this head is green.

- **Shape:** a draft PR to `main`. The first line is `Part of #24061`, with no closing keyword beside any card number in the body. `Clause-②: no` is at a line start in the body and in the changeset. Card and PR assignee: `marchtian`.
- **Done-when item 3:** ruled by the seat at `6236115076`. Two serial reads are the floor, measured and stated in this body; ADR-0049 retired the only contract route. So the card closes `completed` by hand when this PR merges. The first line stays `Part of`, which is why the closing is the seat's act.
- **Premise, measured:** at BASE `b0fe9fad4` the shared prelude is 11 reads in 7 round trips, and `me/*` is 17 in 9, matching the card. At this head both are 8 in 4. HTTP `/get-session` is 10 in 6 on a key read and 8 in 4 while the key is held, and still carries `set-auth-jwt`.
- **The production hunks, read by the seat:**
  - `jwt-key-algorithm.ts`: the `/get-session` hook's matcher additionally requires `answersHttpRequest(context)`. The HTTP door keeps its header, and in-process `auth.api.getSession` calls skip signing. The degrade-on-failure guard is unchanged.
  - `signing-key-read-cache.ts` (new, module-internal) meets both halves of #11633's rule:
    - A `sys_jwks` middleware counts write starts and settles. An entry is served only while both counters equal their values at the read's open and no write is in flight. A read overlapping a write is never stored.
    - A constant `SIGNING_KEY_CACHE_TTL_MS = 30_000`, with no config key.
    - An engine without `registerMiddleware` caches nothing.
  - `internal-field-readback.ts` / `objectql-adapter.ts`: a flagged column is answered from the read's own `where` only for a single, case-sensitive equality on a non-empty string, and only when the column is absent from the row. Every other shape recovers as before.
  - `current-user-endpoints.ts`: behaviour-identical, as recorded in the claim amendment `6236128359`. There is no API-key admission and no tenancy posture, so the session's claim stands as before. `accessToken` and `authGate` stay explicit `undefined` inputs to `assembleExecutionContext`.
- **Out-of-surface files:** `plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts`, the measured producer (the claim's `packages/runtime` hypothesis was falsified), and `plugin-auth/vitest.config.ts`, for `check:test-source-alias`. The claim is amended at `6236128359`, and `domain:cli` is told at `6236133854` on #6024.
- **Negative pins ablated:** four legs, each red, then restored (`git diff HEAD` empty):
  - the matcher's request check;
  - the lookup attach;
  - the `me/*` memo;
  - the write counters.
  The first `me/*` attempt was a tool-refused no-op and was re-run. Only the re-run is counted.
- **Public surface:** built `dist/index.d.ts` / `index.d.mts` of both packages are identical BASE vs head with comments stripped, with a one-type control that reads different. `Clause-②: no` holds, and no contract-review face is hit.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` patch; both publish. Each sentence was checked against the diff:
  - the three-row table matches the body's measurements;
  - "no longer signs a JWT" matches the matcher;
  - "not read back after the session was found by it" matches the lookup attach;
  - "resolve the grants once" matches `resolveAuthzContext`'s memo;
  - "held across requests, under two bounds" matches the cache;
  - "No new configuration key" matches the constant.
- **Gates on this head:** `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success. 28 checks succeeded and 6 were skipped by design (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance). Test Core 2/6 to 6/6 were still running at this read.
- **Accepted deviations:** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3); `test:repo` and the repo-wide lint are CI's.
- **Out-of-scope findings:**
  - The MCP verifier's TTL-only JWKS cache was filed as #24186 (`security`, ungraded).
  - The ADR-0069 gate's second session read, the grant resolver's repeated `sys_user` read (carrier: #15194's territory), and the `handleRequest` re-dispatches are Acceptance notes in this body.
  - The inbound rate limiter's in-process session read is a seat's append to the Acceptance notes.

CI red on head `3e1faaeafe` · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `marchtian` · `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH` · 2026-10-17T16:10Z. The ACCEPT `6236184102` stands. Landing waits for this check.

- **Failing:** `Test Core (5/6)` (job `117435609262`, run `39046277855`), and the aggregate `Test Core` with it. The shard's failed task is `@objectstack/core#test:repo` (`pnpm run test:repo exited (1)`); every other task in the shard passed, `@objectstack/objectql:test` included (437 files, 8236 tests). The other five shards passed.
- **Why it does not read as this diff's (not yet proven):**
  - `core`'s `repo` project is six files (`packages/core/vitest.repo-tests.json`). Each reads fixed sources: `protocol.ts`, `engine.ts`, `relation-filter-lowering.ts`, `import-runner.ts`, and the `packages/**` declaration scans for the operation-private-key helper and `SecurePluginContext`. None of them is a file this PR changes, and none of the symbols those scans look for appears in the diff.
  - `main` at `62c4441efd` and five other PRs this hour (#24184, #24181, #24180, #24178, #24170) were green on all six shards.
  - The shard ran slowly: objectql's import phase alone took 1,490 s.
- **What could not be read:** the failing test's name and message. The job log's `core:test:repo` lines fall outside the 5,000-line tail the MCP log reader returns, and the full-log download is refused from this container.
- **Done in this act:** the one re-run of the failed jobs, on the unchanged head. If it fails again, the failure is treated as this PR's: the dev reproduces `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core run test:repo` on this branch, root-causes it, and fixes it here.

## 席位核对 — patch round 1

ACCEPT extended to head `978ce6133f` · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `marchtian` · `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH` · 2026-10-17T17:22Z. ACCEPT `6236184102` covered `3e1faaeafe`. This extends it over the increment, read by the seat on the diff. It lands through the merge queue once every check on this head is green.

- **Root cause of the red, as the dev reproduced it:** `core`'s `authz-store-unavailable.test.ts` set-equality ledger (`:301`). Moving `makeExecutionContextResolver` onto `resolveAuthzContext` made it a transport the ledger did not list. RED at `4746a55fb` (1 failed of 84), GREEN at `6d7f066f3`.
- **The fix, read by the seat:**
  - The face's catch now returns `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable(err)`, the shared core helper. An authorization-store outage is re-raised to the host's error seam, and every other fault still answers no context.
  - The ledger gains one row, `current-user-endpoints.ts: 'guarded'`. It is classified honestly: the face swallowed the outage before, so a `propagates` row would have been false.
- **The one runtime answer that changes**, stated in the changeset: on a failed permission-store read, `/auth/me/permissions`, `/auth/me/localization` and `/me/apps` answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of a body identical to a signed-out caller's. That is the 2026-08-30 ruling applied to a transport this PR created, in the fail-closed, louder direction. An unprovisioned store still answers the signed-in caller (the control).
- **Pinned and ablated:** `current-user-endpoints-authz-outage.test.ts` turned red on all three routes when the re-raise was replaced (`expected 200 to be 503`), while the control stayed green. Restored: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Citations:** the two bare `#13279` (`allocated-but-absent`) now cite the ruling's live record, commit `6a180e42d` and the test header, with no number guessed. `check-issue-citations` is green.
- **Cross-lane:** the one `packages/core` row was declared to `domain:engine` at `6236850581` on #6367.
- **Gates on this head:** 31 succeeded, 6 skipped by design (the roster set). `Test Core (3/6)` and `Check Changeset` were running at this read. `Test Core (5/6)`, the earlier red shard, succeeded.
- **Card closing:** unchanged. On the item-3 ruling `6236115076`, the seat closes #24061 `completed` at the merge.
